bottleneck: Neural signals drift: neurons shift relative to electrodes, scar tissue forms, and the brain's own plasticity rewires representations, so a decoder calibrated on day one degrades within weeks to months. Users must endure frequent recalibration sessions that interrupt daily life, and long-term non-stationarity remains a core bottleneck for intracranial BCIs. A communication device that needs constant retuning is not a prosthesis but a lab instrument, and the recalibration burden falls on the most disabled users least able to bear it.
current_state: Adaptive decoders that track drift are improving, but eliminating recalibration burden for chronic home use is unsolved. Stability beyond months is rarely demonstrated.

title: BCI decoders decay as neural signals drift
why_it_blocks: Instability turns BCIs from prosthetics into lab instruments requiring technician support. Chronic, calibration-free operation is the precondition for real-world use, and without it adoption stalls at the demonstration stage.
